text: I first wrote to you on 20 August and I still have not had a proper answer about when my assessment will be booked. I understand these things take time but a month with no update is not good enough. Please tell me where it has got to.

Complainant states that when she rang on 9 September the handler she spoke to talked over her, told her she was wasting his time, and put the phone down while she was still speaking. She says she has never been spoken to like that and wants it dealt with by somebody above him.

I am writing on behalf of my brother, who has a learning disability and cannot deal with this himself. He has become very anxious about the letters and has stopped opening the post. I have power of attorney. Please send everything to me at 22 Ferndale Close, WN1 3PL from now on.
I have taken advice from my solicitor and unless I hear back within fourteen days I will be referring this to the ombudsman. I have kept copies of all the correspondence since March.

My neighbour has just handed me a letter from you about my claim. It was addressed to me but delivered to number 47. It has my date of birth and my National Insurance number on it. She has read it. How did this happen?
I made a complaint three weeks ago and nobody has acknowledged it. Now I am being asked to fill in the same form again. The complaints process is worse than the problem I was complaining about.
This is now the sixth time I have written since July. I was told in writing that I would have a final response within eight weeks. That was well over two months ago.

I disagree with the decision on my claim. I do not think the assessor read the report from my consultant properly. I also had to take two unpaid days off work for appointments that were cancelled at short notice, and I want that money back.
